## Summary & Motivation

`start({ hook })` used to throw before enqueuing anything on
single-orchestrator runs. Those runs now admit and bind a start Hook the
way the default engine does. A duplicate is refused without running any
code, and the workflow's `createHook({ token })` gets the Hook that the
admission created.

- **Admission on the queued copy.** Before, a spec 9 delivery that
carried `runInput.startHook` was dropped without writing or running
anything. Now its `run_started` carries the start Hook request, so that
write can admit or refuse the candidate. A candidate never takes turbo,
because turbo would run inline step bodies before that write returns. A
refused candidate is acknowledged without running code. If the World
can't confirm the outcome, the same message is redelivered and never
handed off, so the start Hook request is kept.
- **Echo check on redelivery.** Suppose the admitting `run_started`
committed but its answer was lost, for example to a 503 or a crash. The
redelivery used to find `run_started` in the log and run the code
without checking the token. Now it checks that the loaded run echoes the
token. A missing or mismatched echo fails the run before any code runs.
The span records this check with `workflow.start_hook.trigger=run_load`
rather than `run_started`, so a redelivery no longer looks like another
admission.
- **Holder wake.** A refused duplicate can wake a single-orchestrator
holder stuck pending. That wake goes out on the run's own channel with
`runSpecVersion` and no queue idempotency key, so the key no longer
holds it to one wake per window. Each process now allows one wake per
holder per window and reports later ones as `throttled`. A failed
publish gives the window back.
- **CI.** Nothing in CI ran the `start({ hook })` e2e block at spec 9.
The nextjs-turbopack Postgres lanes (Node and QuickJS) now restart the
built app with `WORKFLOW_SPEC_VERSION=9` and run the block again.
`WORKFLOW_E2E_EXPECT_START_HOOK=1` makes the block fail instead of skip
when the World lacks `atomicStartHook`.

Spec 9 is still opt-in via `WORKFLOW_SPEC_VERSION=9`. The start Hook
flags for each World are unchanged.

## Test Plan

Tests added. Locally, the core typecheck and unit suite pass. The
`start({ hook })` e2e block passes at spec 9 on nextjs-turbopack against
both the Local World and the Postgres World, on the Node and QuickJS
VMs. The new CI step was also run by hand against Postgres: it passed,
and every run it created was stamped spec 9.

[core] Bind start({ hook }) on the single-orchestrator engine (#5156)

## Summary & Motivation

`start({ hook })` used to throw before enqueuing anything on
single-orchestrator runs. Those runs now admit and bind a start Hook the
way the default engine does. A duplicate is refused without running any
code, and the workflow's `createHook({ token })` gets the Hook that the
admission created.

- **Admission on the queued copy.** Before, a spec 9 delivery that
carried `runInput.startHook` was dropped without writing or running
anything. Now its `run_started` carries the start Hook request, so that
write can admit or refuse the candidate. A candidate never takes turbo,
because turbo would run inline step bodies before that write returns. A
refused candidate is acknowledged without running code. If the World
can't confirm the outcome, the same message is redelivered and never
handed off, so the start Hook request is kept.
- **Echo check on redelivery.** Suppose the admitting `run_started`
committed but its answer was lost, for example to a 503 or a crash. The
redelivery used to find `run_started` in the log and run the code
without checking the token. Now it checks that the loaded run echoes the
token. A missing or mismatched echo fails the run before any code runs.
The span records this check with `workflow.start_hook.trigger=run_load`
rather than `run_started`, so a redelivery no longer looks like another
admission.
- **Holder wake.** A refused duplicate can wake a single-orchestrator
holder stuck pending. That wake goes out on the run's own channel with
`runSpecVersion` and no queue idempotency key, so the key no longer
holds it to one wake per window. Each process now allows one wake per
holder per window and reports later ones as `throttled`. A failed
publish gives the window back.
- **CI.** Nothing in CI ran the `start({ hook })` e2e block at spec 9.
The nextjs-turbopack Postgres lanes (Node and QuickJS) now restart the
built app with `WORKFLOW_SPEC_VERSION=9` and run the block again.
`WORKFLOW_E2E_EXPECT_START_HOOK=1` makes the block fail instead of skip
when the World lacks `atomicStartHook`.

Spec 9 is still opt-in via `WORKFLOW_SPEC_VERSION=9`. The start Hook
flags for each World are unchanged.

## Test Plan

Tests added. Locally, the core typecheck and unit suite pass. The
`start({ hook })` e2e block passes at spec 9 on nextjs-turbopack against
both the Local World and the Postgres World, on the Node and QuickJS
VMs. The new CI step was also run by hand against Postgres: it passed,
and every run it created was stamped spec 9.
